title: Count up
prompt: Using a recursive CTE, show the numbers from 1 up to the number of books, in a column named n. Replace the ___ with the stopping condition.
hints: Keep going while n is below the count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: WITH RECURSIVE c(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM c WHERE n < (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books)) SELECT n FROM c;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH RECURSIVE c(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM c WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM c;
WITH RECURSIVE c(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM c WHERE n <= (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books)) SELECT n FROM c;

title: Up the chain
prompt: Starting from the employee with no manager, walk down the org chart. Show each reachable employee's name and depth, with the top at 0.
hints: Start with manager_id IS NULL, then join reports.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (SELECT id, name, 0 AS depth FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name, c.depth + 1 FROM employees e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id) SELECT name, depth FROM chain;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, 0 AS depth FROM employees;

WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (SELECT id, name, 0 AS depth FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name, c.depth FROM employees e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id) SELECT name, depth FROM chain;

title: Generate dates
prompt: Generate every date from 2024-03-01 to 2024-03-05 in a column named day, then count readings per day as readings, including 0.
hints: Generate dates recursively, then LEFT JOIN.
solutions: WITH RECURSIVE d(day) AS (SELECT '2024-03-01' UNION ALL SELECT date(day, '+1 day') FROM d WHERE day < '2024-03-05') SELECT d.day, COUNT(r.id) AS readings FROM d LEFT JOIN readings r ON r.reading_date = d.day GROUP BY d.day;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT reading_date AS day, COUNT(*) AS readings FROM readings GROUP BY reading_date;

WITH RECURSIVE d(day) AS (SELECT '2024-03-01' UNION ALL SELECT date(day, '+1 day') FROM d WHERE day < '2024-03-05') SELECT d.day, COUNT(*) AS readings FROM d LEFT JOIN readings r ON r.reading_date = d.day GROUP BY d.day;

title: Everyone invited by
prompt: Show the username of everyone directly or indirectly invited by user 1. Don't include user 1.
hints: Start from user 1's direct invitees, then keep walking.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE users SET referrer_id = 1 WHERE id = 5; INSERT INTO users VALUES (6, 'sage', 5, '2024-01-15');

solutions: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE referrer_id = 1 UNION ALL SELECT u.id, u.username FROM users u JOIN t ON u.referrer_id = t.id) SELECT username FROM t;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT username FROM users WHERE referrer_id = 1;
WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE id = 1 UNION ALL SELECT u.id, u.username FROM users u JOIN t ON u.referrer_id = t.id) SELECT username FROM t;

title: A broken chain
prompt: Hugo's manager no longer exists, so he isn't reachable from the top. Show the name of employees who aren't reached when walking down from anyone with no manager.
hints: Walk the chart, then find who's missing.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (SELECT id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id FROM employees e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id) SELECT name FROM employees WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM chain);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL;

WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (SELECT id FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id FROM employees e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id) SELECT name FROM employees WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM chain);

title: Fix the endless query
prompt: This should show level from 1 up to the number of departments, but its stopping condition is missing, so it would never end. Replace the ___ to fix it.
hints: Add a condition to the recursive part.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: WITH RECURSIVE c(level) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT level + 1 FROM c WHERE level < (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM departments)) SELECT level FROM c;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH RECURSIVE c(level) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT level + 1 FROM c WHERE level < 2) SELECT level FROM c;
WITH RECURSIVE c(level) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT level + 1 FROM c WHERE level <= (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM departments)) SELECT level FROM c;
